Give an LLM too much detail, and you’ve already designed the solution. Give it too little, and it fills in the gaps with assumptions. 

Finding that balance is surprisingly difficult.

I’ve found the most effective approach is to treat AI like a collaborative thinking partner

When I have a new idea, I’ll spend time in an AI-assisted requirements session. I’ll ask questions, explore edge cases, challenge assumptions and gradually build a shared understanding of the problem.

Set expectations from the start.

I’ll explicitly say things like:

* This is an early concept.

* Keep the discussion high level.
* Don’t dive into implementation yet.
* Ask questions if something is unclear.
* Help me explore the idea before proposing solutions.

Without those guardrails, it’s remarkable how quickly the conversation jumps into architecture diagrams, database schemas and code
